etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English donacion, donation, from Middle French donation, from Latin dōnātiō (“a present”), from dōnō (“to give”), from dōnum (“a gift”). Recorded in English since the 15th century.

definitions.definition: A voluntary gift or contribution for a specific cause.

quote.citation: 1610–1611 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tempest”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene i]:
quote.text: And some donation freely to estateOn the bless'd lovers.

definitions.definition: The act of giving or bestowing; a grant.

quote.citation: 1692–1717, Robert South, Twelve Sermons Preached upon Several Occasions, volume (please specify |volume=I to VI), London:
quote.text: After donation there is an absolute change and alienation of the property of the thing given.
